html:
An ancient city in the northern Punjab, near today's Rawalpindi in Pakistan, founded around 1000 BCE. It stood where roads from Central Asia and Persia met the road into the Ganges plain.

That position made it rich and often conquered. It fell under Achaemenid Persia after the Persian advance to the Indus. Its king welcomed Alexander the Great in 326 BCE. It then became a provincial seat of the Maurya Empire, where Ashoka served as governor before he was emperor.

Taxila was famous as a place of learning. Tradition links it with the grammarian Panini and with Chanakya, adviser to Chandragupta Maurya. Students came to study medicine, law and the Vedas with private teachers, rather than at a single university.

Later rulers left three city sites: Bhir Mound, Sirkap, built in the Greek grid style of the Indo-Greeks, and Sirsukh. Under the Kushans it was a centre of Gandharan Buddhist art. Hun raids in the 5th century ruined it. It is a World Heritage Site.
sum: An ancient city in the northern Punjab, near today's Rawalpindi in Pakistan, founded around 1000 BCE. It stood where roads from Central Asia and Persia met the road into the Ganges plain.
